title: Data Modeling and Database Design
name: 4. Data Modeling and Database Design
description: Master relational database design and analytical dimensional modeling: conceptual, logical, and physical models, Crow's Foot ERDs, 1NF/2NF/3NF/BCNF, Star/Snowflake schemas, fact table grain, SCD Type 1 & 2, and event-driven architectures.

quiz.question: What is the primary requirement of First Normal Form (1NF)?
options: Eliminating foreign keys
Every column must contain atomic (indivisible) values with no repeating groups
Creating a snowflake schema
Every table must have a surrogate key
quiz.explanation: 1NF requires that each column contains atomic values, each cell holds a single value, and repeating groups or arrays are eliminated into separate rows.

quiz.question: When does a table violate Second Normal Form (2NF)?
options: When it has too many columns
When a non-key attribute depends on only part of a composite candidate key (partial dependency)
When it uses VARCHAR instead of TEXT
When foreign keys allow NULL values
quiz.explanation: 2NF is violated when a composite key exists and a non-key attribute depends functionally on only a subset of that composite key rather than the entire key.

quiz.question: What characterizes a Transitive Dependency in Third Normal Form (3NF)?
options: A foreign key referencing another schema
A non-key attribute functionally depending on another non-key attribute (X → Y → Z)
An index slowing down write operations
A table with multiple primary keys
quiz.explanation: 3NF eliminates transitive dependencies where non-key attribute A determines non-key attribute B (e.g. employee_id → department_id → department_name).

quiz.question: What is the primary architectural difference between a Star Schema and a Snowflake Schema?
options: Star schemas have no fact tables
In a star schema, dimension tables are denormalized; in a snowflake schema, dimensions are normalized into hierarchies
Snowflake schemas cannot store measures
Star schemas only work in PostgreSQL
quiz.explanation: Star schemas maintain denormalized dimensions connecting directly to a central fact table. Snowflake schemas normalize dimension hierarchies (e.g. Product → Subcategory → Category).

quiz.question: Why is SCD Type 2 the standard pattern for dimension history in data warehouses?
options: It overwrites old values to save disk space
It creates a new dimension row with effective date bounds and active flags, preserving exact historical context for older transactions
It deletes old records automatically
It prevents all updates completely
quiz.explanation: SCD Type 2 inserts a new row with effective_from, effective_to, and is_current flags, allowing historical sales to remain associated with the customer's state at the time of purchase.
